name: Register Bitfield Editor
blurb: toggle bits of a hex value and read each field's meaning
intro: Decodes a register value into named fields (value = (reg >> lsb) & mask), shows what each field's code means, flips bits when you click them, and writes CMSIS-style _Pos/_Msk macros. Describe the fields one per line as NAME msb:lsb followed by code=meaning pairs, or pick a preset register.

inputs.label: Value
inputs.help: Leave empty to use the preset's typical value.

inputs.label: Flip bits
inputs.help: Bit numbers to toggle; clicking a bit in the drawing does the same to the value.

examples.title: BME280 ctrl_meas: normal mode, x1 oversampling

usage: Give the value (0x hex, 0b binary or decimal), the width (8/16/32) and a field list (one per line: NAME msb:lsb then code=meaning pairs), or a preset (aircr, tccr1b, usartcr1); optionally bit numbers to flip. It returns the value in hex, decimal and binary, a table of each field's value and meaning, result.bits and result.fields, warnings for set bits outside any field and overlapping fields, and C _Pos/_Msk macros. Use it to decode a register dump or to compose a value to write.
sources: Field extraction: value = (reg >> lsb) & (2^width - 1); macro style from Arm CMSIS-Core
